cases.angle: Under-redaction: every one of the 23 names in CREDENTIAL_KEYS with a realistic 28-char secret, in three shapes (`key=v`, `key: v`, UPPER env `KEY=v`) — 69 attempts.
cases.expectedBehavior: All 69 deliver `<key>=[redacted]`; no attempt ships `deadbeefcafe0123456789abcdef`.
cases.observedBehavior: 69/69 redacted. secret, secrets, password, passwd, passphrase, token, api_key, apikey, api-key, access_key, secret_key, secret_access_key, private_key, client_secret, access_token, refresh_token, id_token, session_token, auth_token, bearer_token, credential, credentials, authorization — all three shapes, all cases folded (the regex is /gi).

cases.angle: Under-redaction: separator-delimited vendor prefixes and the credential-only suffix vocabulary.
cases.expectedBehavior: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, my_api_key_value, openai_api_key, x-api-key, MY-SECRET-VALUE, acme_client_secret_b64, svc_token_string, a_b_c_secret all redact.
cases.observedBehavior: 9/9 redacted. The mirror image also holds: max_tokens=200000, token_count: 8192, auth_expired and oauth survive untouched (case G5-2a).

cases.angle: Under-redaction: JSON double-quoted, single-quoted, unbalanced quote, unbalanced quote followed by prose, quoted value containing spaces, multi-line, quoted key inside JSON with whitespace variants.
cases.expectedBehavior: Every shape redacts; an unbalanced quote must fail closed (redact to end of line, never redact nothing).
cases.observedBehavior: All redact. `token="deadbeef… and then more` -> `token="[redacted]` (fails closed, consuming the trailing prose). `password: "<secret> more words"` -> `password: "[redacted]"`. `{\n  "password": "<secret>"\n}` -> redacted. `{ "credentials" :  { "token" :   "<secret>" } }` redacts the inner secret but mangles the structural `{` (see G5-2e / defect G5-D3).

cases.angle: Under-redaction: a secret pasted into the structured CODE field, which also reaches the chat surface.
cases.expectedBehavior: The code is normalized, then redacted, then bounded.
cases.observedBehavior: code `sk_live_deadbeefcafe0123` -> `[redacted]`, text `[redacted]: m`. code `secret=deadbeefcafe0123456` -> `secret=[redacted]`. code `resource_gone` untouched. A 4000-char code is truncated to 64 + `…` and the notice stays under 400 chars.

cases.angle: Under-redaction: a secret (and a credential KEY) split by control characters — NUL inside the value, NUL inside the key name, NUL between key and `=`, U+200B inside a vendor prefix.
cases.expectedBehavior: stripControl runs BEFORE redaction on the reporting path, so every reassembled key/secret is caught.
cases.observedBehavior: Through describeFailure (the only path a notice takes): `sec\u0000ret=<secret>` -> `secret=[redacted]`; `tok\u0000en=<secret>` -> `token=[redacted]`; `secret\u0000=<secret>` -> `secret=[redacted]`; `sk_live_dead\u0000beef…` and `sk_live_dead\u200bbeef…` -> `[redacted]`; a pure control-character buffer falls through to the gateway framing instead of an empty diagnosis. Note: redactSecrets() called directly on `sec\u0000ret=<secret>` does NOT redact — correct by design, because normalization is the caller's documented precondition and every production caller honours it.

cases.angle: Under-redaction: a state word used as a PREFIX of a real secret, plus casing variants of the state words.
cases.expectedBehavior: `secret=missing_but_actually_deadbeefcafe` must redact (it is not the state word `missing`); `secret=missing` must survive.
cases.observedBehavior: `secret=missing_but_actually_deadbeefcafe` -> `secret=[redacted]`; `token=expired_deadbeefcafe0123` -> `token=[redacted]`; `secret=short` -> `secret=[redacted]`. Casing variants (`secret=MISSING`, `secret=Missing`, `token=UNSET`) survive — the state-word set is matched case-insensitively, which is the documented intent, not a leak of a credential shape.

cases.angle: Under-redaction: vendor discriminators and header values with no key name at all.
cases.expectedBehavior: sk_live_, sk_test_, sk-ant-, ghp_, github_pat_, xoxb-, xoxp-, a JWT triplet, `Bearer <v>` and `Basic <v>` all redact.
cases.observedBehavior: 11/11 redacted. `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` -> `Authorization: [redacted] [redacted]` (the scheme word is consumed by the credential-key rule after the header rule already replaced the token; cosmetic, no leak).

cases.angle: Under-redaction: a secret placed so that the 240-char MESSAGE_LIMIT cut lands inside it (pads 225/228/230/232/235/240) plus a vendor shape at the boundary.
cases.expectedBehavior: Redaction runs before truncation, so no partial secret can survive the cut.

cases.angle: Under-redaction: a credential key preceded by URL punctuation instead of whitespace/brace/quote.
cases.expectedBehavior: `?access_token=<secret>` is an exact credential key with a value and must redact.
cases.observedBehavior: LEAK, delivered verbatim to the chat surface. `[turn failed] spawn_failed: gjc: POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages?access_token=sk9deadbeefcafe0123456789 -> 401 unauthorized. Send /new to rebind this conversation.` Same for `?api_key=deadbeefcafe0123456789&limit=10` and `#token=deadbeefcafe0123456789`. CREDENTIAL_KEY's left boundary is `(?:^|[\s,{(\["'])`, and `?`, `&`, `#`, `/` are not in it. Defect G5-D1.

cases.angle: Under-redaction: a credential key whose JSON value is an array or an object.
cases.expectedBehavior: `{"secrets":["<secret>","<secret2>"]}` must not deliver either secret.
cases.observedBehavior: LEAK. Output: `{"secrets":[redacted]"deadbeefcafe0123456789","hunter2trombone"]}` — the bare rule consumed the `[` as the whole value, so both secrets ship in the clear and the structural token is redacted instead. Same for `{"credentials":["<secret>"]}`. Defect G5-D3.

cases.angle: Under-redaction: an unquoted credential value that contains whitespace.
cases.expectedBehavior: No part of the credential reaches the surface.
cases.observedBehavior: PARTIAL LEAK. `password=p@ss w0rd was rejected by the keychain` -> `password=[redacted] w0rd was rejected…`; `passphrase=correct horse battery staple` -> `passphrase=[redacted] horse battery staple`. The bare rule is one whitespace-delimited token by design; a spaced passphrase leaks all but its first word. Defect G5-D4 (low).

cases.angle: Under-redaction: a PEM private-key block, which carries no key=value and no vendor discriminator.
cases.expectedBehavior: Not covered by the two declared recognisers, so a miss here is a scope statement rather than a broken rule.
cases.observedBehavior: Delivered verbatim: `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEowIBAAKCAQEA9deadbeefcafe0123456789\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`. Recorded as a residual gap (observations), not a defect: the design explicitly recognises exact key names and vendor shapes only, and a gjc failure blob printing a PEM body is not an observed shape.

cases.expectedBehavior: Byte-identical output — the diagnosis is what #14 exists to deliver.

cases.angle: Over-redaction: snake_case/kebab identifiers that literally BEGIN with sk_/pk_/rk_ (the assignment's `snake_case identifiers containing sk_/rk_/pk_` angle).

cases.angle: Over-redaction: the documented exemption — a lowercase snake_case code or a named state word after a real credential key.
cases.expectedBehavior: `authorization: insufficient scope for this operation, ask the owner`, `token: expired 4 minutes ago`, `secret: missing from the keychain entry`, `authorization=insufficient_scope_for_this_operation` all survive.

cases.angle: The other side of that exemption: a real credential that happens to be lowercase snake_case.
cases.expectedBehavior: Declared behaviour: `secret=missing` survives, `secret=short` is redacted — the exemption is by value vocabulary/shape, so a snake_case-shaped secret is knowingly exempt.

This is the documented, deliberate tradeoff in the rebuilt design (isDiagnosticWord's `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)+$` branch), so it is reported as a residual risk rather than a defect. Real provider keys (mixed case, digits, no underscore grouping, or a vendor discriminator) do not match it; a human passphrase like `correct_horse_battery_staple` does.

cases.angle: Over-redaction: a `{` immediately after a credential key.

cases.observedBehavior: `{"credentials": {"file": "/Users/x/creds.json"}} could not be read` -> `{"credentials": [redacted]"file": "/Users/x/creds.json"}} could not be read`; `token: {status: expired, age: 4m}` -> `token: [redacted] expired, age: 4m}` (loses `status:`). cases.angle: Cap: the deliberately permitted shape — a failing turn (fail + successful replay) alternating with a fully clean turn.

In the 5-driver variant one turn surfaced `resource_gone` and four succeeded on the rebound session; epoch 1.

cases.angle: No-replay guard: trailing prose, trailing unterminated JSON frame, tool_execution_start then death, assistant text then failure, output tokens only, stderr-only failure, whitespace-only tail, prose containing a mid-string brace, leading-space unterminated frame.

REFUSED with `turn_not_replayed` (1 turn spawn) and evidence named: unterminated frame (`an unterminated frame from a child that died mid-write`), 1 tool call(s), `assistant text, 7 output token(s)`, `2 output token(s)`, leading-space unterminated frame. Every refusal still rebound to e1, so the next turn works. GjcTurnStream.pending probes: `''`/spaces/`prose`/`}`/`[` -> false; `{"a":1`, ` \n {"a":1`, `{"a":1}` -> true (a newline-less complete frame is conservatively pending, which is the safe direction).

cases.angle: Config: fresh home, valid file, chmod 000, directory, dangling symlink, symlink to a valid file, zero-byte, JSON array, JSON null, JSON string, truncated JSON, wrong schemaVersion — each at BOOT (loadConfig) and at RELOAD (reloadConfig against a live config carrying mentionAllowlist+channels).
cases.expectedBehavior: ENOENT with no directory entry means defaults at BOOT only; every other shape refuses at boot and keeps the previous config at reload.
cases.observedBehavior: 12/12 correct. BOOT: fresh home -> defaults; valid and symlink-to-valid -> loaded; chmod 000 -> `unreadable (EACCES); refusing to start on defaults`; directory -> `unreadable (EISDIR)`; DANGLING SYMLINK -> `unreadable (ENOENT); refusing to start on defaults` (the generation-4 fail-open is closed by lstat); zero-byte and truncated -> `could not parse`; array/null/string -> `config must be an object`; schemaVersion 2 -> `schemaVersion must be 1`. RELOAD: every shape including the fresh home returns ok:false, keeps `mentionAllowlist=["live-user"]`, and reports one config_invalid diagnostic ending `; keeping the previous configuration`.

cases.angle: Config: config.json unlinked between two reloads issued in the same tick.
cases.expectedBehavior: The reload that sees the file applies it; the one that does not keeps the live policy and reports. No half-applied state either way.

A subsequent BOOT on the same now-empty home correctly falls back to defaults, confirming the requireFile split is the only difference between the two callers.

cases.angle: Config: a file editing reloadable, restart-only and unconsumed fields at once.
cases.expectedBehavior: changed = live fields only; restart-only reported and NOT applied; unconsumed reported as ignored.
cases.observedBehavior: changed=[mentionAllowlist,debounceMs]; restartRequired=[socketPath,turnTimeoutMs,model,webhook]; ignored=[logVerbosity]. The published config kept the old socketPath and logVerbosity=info while taking the new allowlist and debounce.

cases.angle: Config: the boot entrypoint as a real process with an unreadable config — the launchd crash-loop angle.

cases.expectedBehavior: Non-zero exit with the reason on stderr, not an unhandled rejection stack.

No stack, no `error: Unhandled`. Dangling-symlink home: EXIT=1, `… is unreadable (ENOENT); refusing to start on defaults`. Wrong subcommand still exits 2 with the usage line.

cases.angle: #13/#14 end to end: 10 failure kinds driven through chat.send over a real listening unix socket, comparing the DELIVERED chat.message text with the logged line.
cases.expectedBehavior: The delivered notice carries the runtime's own code and message, is identical to the logged string, and is byte-equal to formatFailureNotice(error).
cases.observedBehavior: 10/10 identical (logged===delivered true in every case) and equal to formatFailureNotice. Examples: `[turn failed] resource_gone: session endpoint record is gone. Send /new to rebind this conversation.`; `[turn failed] unsupported_state_version: state moved` (genuine, no hint); `[turn failed] gjc turn exited 137:` (killed child, never erased to a bare `[turn failed]`); `[turn failed] spawn_failed: env AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=[redacted] rejected; token=[redacted]. Send /new to rebind this conversation.`

cases.angle: #14 hint policy: the four rebindable codes plus rebind_cap_exceeded get the `/new` hint; `turn_not_replayed` must NOT.
cases.expectedBehavior: turn_not_replayed carries no `/new` hint (the automatic rebind already happened; a second reset would discard the fresh binding).
cases.observedBehavior: Hint present for resource_gone, spawn_failed, terminal_uncertain, managed_append_identity_mismatch, rebind_cap_exceeded. Hint ABSENT for turn_not_replayed over the socket: `[turn failed] turn_not_replayed: resource_gone: rebound to e2, not replayed` — asserted `not.toContain('/new')`. Also absent for unfamiliar codes, `RESOURCE_GONE` (case is not folded), and codeless errors. ` resource_gone ` with transport whitespace still gets the hint. The hint is period-separated and is not appended twice when the message already ends in `.`

cases.expectedBehavior: `/new` calls forgetRebinds for the exact origin key; `gateway.reloadConfig` and SIGHUP go through one implementation and log the same applied/restart-required/ignored breakdown.

After chmod 000 the verb returned ok:false with the keep-previous diagnostic, and a SIGHUP raised on the same server logged the identical failure through the same code path.

defects.title: A credential in a URL query or fragment is delivered verbatim: the credential-key left boundary excludes `?`, `&` and `#`
defects.contract: #14 'only secrets redacted' (the redaction half: an exact credential key with a value must be redacted)
defects.repro: formatFailureNotice(new GjcRuntimeError('gjc turn exited 1', { code: 'spawn_failed', message: 'gjc: POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages?access_token=sk9deadbeefcafe0123456789 -> 401 unauthorized' }))
defects.observed: `[turn failed] spawn_failed: gjc: POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages?access_token=sk9deadbeefcafe0123456789 -> 401 unauthorized. Send /new to rebind this conversation.` — the token ships to the chat surface. Same for `GET /v1/sessions?api_key=deadbeefcafe0123456789&limit=10 -> 403` and `https://x/y#token=deadbeefcafe0123456789`. The identical key with a space or brace before it redacts, so this is purely the delimiter class.
defects.expected: `?`, `&`, `#` and `/` are as much a key delimiter as a space; a query-string credential is the most common way a real HTTP failure line carries one.
defects.impact: An upstream 401/403 line — exactly the failure #14 exists to surface — leaks a provider credential to Discord/Telegram and to the delivery ledger. Realistic for any provider that accepts a token as a query parameter.
defects.test: /tmp/rt-defects.test.ts 'confirmed leaks on the real notice surface'

defects.title: Any identifier beginning with sk_/pk_/rk_ and 12+ following characters is erased, destroying the whole diagnosis
defects.contract: #14 'only secrets redacted — a runtime code or a file path is the whole diagnosis'
defects.observed: `[redacted] while draining the queue`, delivered as `[turn failed] spawn_failed: [redacted] while draining the queue.` Also `pk_index_rebuild_failed at step 3`, `rk_queue_drain_timeout after 30s`, `sk-server-restart-required`, `sk_pool_exhausted`. Measured boundary: `sk_` + 11 chars survives, `sk_` + 12 chars is redacted, so the rule is a length coin-flip on ordinary identifiers.
defects.expected: Only a vendor discriminator should trigger the shape rule (`sk_live_`, `sk_test_`, `sk-ant-`, `sk_proj_`, `sk_api_` — already covered by the preceding, discriminated pattern). A bare two-letter prefix plus a snake_case word is an identifier, not a key.
defects.impact: Diagnosis loss in the direction the rebuild explicitly set out to remove: the notice becomes `[redacted] while draining the queue`, which is the zero-diagnosis line #14 exists to eliminate. `\b` only protects prefixes that appear INSIDE a word (disk_, risk_, task_); an identifier that starts with sk_/pk_/rk_ has no protection.
defects.test: /tmp/rt-defects.test.ts 'over-redaction on the real notice surface' and /tmp/rt-redact-over.test.ts 'snake sk_'

defects.title: A structural `{` or `[` after a credential key is consumed as the value: array/object-valued credentials leak while the JSON structure is corrupted
defects.contract: #14 'only secrets redacted' — broken in BOTH directions by one rule
defects.repro: redactSecrets('{"secrets":["deadbeefcafe0123456789","hunter2trombone"]}') and redactSecrets('{"credentials": {"file": "/Users/x/creds.json"}} could not be read')
defects.observed: `{"secrets":[redacted]"deadbeefcafe0123456789","hunter2trombone"]}` — BOTH secrets are delivered in the clear while the `[` is replaced. `{"credentials": [redacted]"file": "/Users/x/creds.json"}}` loses the nested key name. `token: {status: expired, age: 4m}` -> `token: [redacted] expired, age: 4m}` loses `status:`. Nested object form (`{ "credentials" : { "token" : "<secret>" } }`) still redacts the inner secret because the inner key matches, but an ARRAY has no inner key and nothing rescues it.
defects.expected: A brace or bracket is not a value. Either skip structural openers (leaving the nested keys to match on their own) or treat the balanced region as the value.
defects.impact: A runtime that dumps a credential list (`{"secrets":[…]}`) delivers every entry verbatim, and the structural corruption makes a JSON blob harder to read at the same time. Lower likelihood than G5-D1 but the same class of leak.

defects.title: An unquoted credential value containing spaces leaks every word after the first
defects.observed: `passphrase=[redacted] horse battery staple`; `password=p@ss w0rd was rejected by the keychain` -> `password=[redacted] w0rd was rejected by the keychain`.
defects.expected: For `passphrase`/`password` specifically, an unquoted value plausibly runs to end of line; at minimum the residue should not be a readable fragment of the credential.
defects.impact: Partial credential disclosure. Low because a runtime normally quotes or omits a spaced value, and the first token is already gone — but a human passphrase is exactly the shape that survives.
defects.test: /tmp/rt-defects.test.ts 'confirmed leaks on the real notice surface'

observations: The generation-4 defects are all closed at abf6919: the exempt-word smuggling hole (G4-D1) is gone because key names are now an exact list, the vendor-prefix destruction of prose and codes (G4-D2/G4-D4) is gone for every string in the 31-case survival matrix except the sk_/pk_/rk_ family (G5-D2), the unbalanced-quote fail-open (G4-D3) now fails closed, and the dangling-symlink boot fail-open (G4-D5) is refused with `unreadable (ENOENT); refusing to start on defaults`.

The snake_case value exemption is a knowing tradeoff, reported as a residual risk rather than a defect: `secret=hunter2trombone_x1` and `authorization=my_super_secret_value` are delivered verbatim because isDiagnosticWord exempts `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)+$`. Provider-issued keys do not match that shape; human passphrases and word-list secrets do.

State-word casing variants (`secret=MISSING`, `secret=Missing`, `token=UNSET`) survive by design — CREDENTIAL_STATE_WORDS is matched after toLowerCase(). Verified as intended behaviour, not a leak of a credential shape.

redactSecrets() alone does not catch a credential KEY split by a control character (`sec\u0000ret=<secret>`); every production caller runs stripControl first (describeFailure/firstDiagnosis), and through that path all five smuggling attempts are redacted. Documented precondition, not a defect.

A PEM private-key block is not covered by either recogniser and is delivered verbatim. Out of the declared scope (exact key names + vendor discriminators) and not an observed gjc output shape, so recorded here rather than as a defect.

Alternating-pattern receipt as requested: 10 turns with 5 failing produced epoch 5, five rebinds, every consecutive counter reading `1/3`, and `lifetime=1,2,3,4,5`. A 12-round variant produced the same half-rate growth. The lifetime field is the only thing that makes the pattern visible, and it does.

The cap now genuinely bounds the shape it was built for: a turn-level failure that recurs every turn and whose replay succeeds stops at epoch 3 and then fails explicitly forever, because a replayed turn does not clear the budget. Concurrency (6 in-flight failing turns on one origin) spends exactly one rebind.

Repo suite at abf6919: bun test packages/gateway = 135 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail / 617 expect(), matching the leader receipt. /tmp/rt-cap2.test.ts is retained for the B2 alternating log evidence; its A2/C2 assertions were mis-specified scenarios (the stub let a clean first attempt clear the budget) and are superseded by /tmp/rt-cap3.test.ts, which drives the recurring failure correctly.

The four defects are all inside redactSecrets.
